ordinary_canyonlands.intro: I’d keep this deliberately unhurried, but I need your visit dates before I can turn it into a sound three-day Canyonlands plan. The one named sunset stop I can verify here—Grand View Point—has a weekday closure Monday through Thursday from July 27 through October 1; it is only usable Friday through Sunday, with limited parking. The park also warns that entrance, overlook, and trailhead parking can fill, so a relaxed photography day is best built around one district rather than crisscrossing the park. rv_glacier_before.intro: I’d make this a two-base, low-driving trip: two relaxed days around Apgar and the West Glacier entrance, then move the RV to the St. Mary side by an RV-legal route outside the park for two more days. The key correction is that your 24-foot RV is over the 21-foot limit for the restricted portion of Going-to-the-Sun Road, so none of these days asks you to drive that corridor or cross the park over Logan Pass. Logan Pass should only be considered separately if the alpine road is open and you have a legal smaller vehicle or an operating shuttle; it is not part of this RV itinerary. For an early-October trip, do not count on Going-to-the-Sun Road’s alpine section being open. Temporary alpine closures can occur, and there is no date-specific opening guarantee here, so check the NPS road-status page immediately before attempting any alpine access. Also verify early-October visitor-center hours, since current operating status is not established. For 2026, NPS says vehicle reservations are not required. You will still need valid park admission; if anyone in the party is a non-U.S. resident age 16 or older, NPS lists an additional $100 nonresident fee unless admission is covered by an Annual or America the Beautiful Pass.

stops.name: Apgar Visitor Center ranger orientation
stops.note: Start at the west-side shuttle hub and ask rangers about current road conditions, early-October services, and any legal non-RV transportation operating during your visit. Confirm hours before setting out.
stops.why: This gives you reliable same-day guidance without putting the 24-foot RV onto the restricted Going-to-the-Sun Road corridor.

stops.name: Apgar Visitor Center exhibits
stops.note: Spend an unhurried session with the visitor-center exhibits. Treat this as the day’s interpretive experience rather than trying to force an uncertain alpine drive.
stops.why: It provides a real park experience on the west side while keeping the first day gentle.

stops.name: West Glacier entrance gateway
stops.note: Use the entrance area as a relaxed gateway visit and photography session. Remain on roads and pullouts where the RV is legally allowed, and do not continue onto the restricted Going-to-the-Sun Road corridor.
stops.why: This is a distinct west-side sightseeing experience that works with the RV rather than depending on alpine access.

stops.name: Apgar Visitor Center shuttle-hub visit
stops.note: Return specifically to understand any same-day transportation options that may be operating. This is informational only: early-October shuttle service has not been verified, so do not build the day around it.
stops.why: It lets you assess optional non-RV access without presenting a shuttle or Logan Pass trip as guaranteed.

stops.name: Trail of the Cedars
stops.note: Walk the accessible forest loop through an old-growth cedar and hemlock grove, with time to enjoy the creek gorge and interpretive features.
stops.why: Adds a substantial, easy nature walk on the west side of Glacier without repeating either existing visit.

stops.name: McDonald Creek Overlook
stops.note: Stop for views of McDonald Creek and its rushing turquoise water from the designated overlook.
stops.why: Adds a distinct scenic viewpoint that fits naturally with the day's West Glacier and Apgar locations.

constrained_olympic_before.intro: I’d make this a three-landscape Olympic trip: an alpine sunrise at Hurricane Ridge, a rain-forest day at Hoh, and a coastal-feeling sunset stop around Kalaloch. That gives you distinctly different park settings without treating a visitor center as the day’s main event. Because no lodging base or dates are set, I’ve kept the order flexible rather than pretending the cross-park drives are short; choose the day order around where you sleep. For your easy-walk preference, these are intentionally light, with time for exhibits, photography, and unhurried outdoor viewing rather than a long hike. I couldn’t verify distances or current access for specific trails, so treat any added trail walk as a same-day choice after checking conditions. Hoh deserves an especially early start: the park warns that entrance waits from 7:30 AM to 5 PM can run 1–3+ hours when parking fills. Hurricane Ridge facilities and road access should also be checked the day you go, since the contact station’s hours are not confirmed here.

stops.name: Sunrise at Hurricane Ridge
stops.note: Make the high-country setting your morning anchor: settle in for changing early light and broad scenic viewing at your own pace. Confirm same-day road access and conditions before committing to the sunrise drive.
stops.why: This is the trip’s clearest alpine contrast to the rainforest and coast.

stops.name: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Contact Station
stops.note: Use the ranger contact point for orientation and a conditions check. Rangers are present during open summer hours, but there is no indoor visitor space or running water at the station.
stops.why: A useful, low-key reset after sunrise before deciding whether an additional short walk feels worthwhile.

stops.name: Hurricane Ridge scenic afternoon
stops.note: Keep the afternoon open for relaxed viewing and photography in the Hurricane Ridge area rather than forcing a long trail. Choose only a short outing whose conditions and distance you can confirm that day.
stops.why: It preserves an easy pace and leaves room for weather-driven decisions.

days.label: Rain forest and a slow Hoh day

stops.name: Early arrival at Hoh Rain Forest
stops.note: Arrive before the main daytime entrance period if practical, then let the forest atmosphere—not a packed trail list—set the pace. The park warns of lengthy entrance delays between 7:30 AM and 5 PM when parking fills.
stops.why: Starting early is the most practical way to protect the relaxed part of the day.

stops.name: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center
stops.note: Browse exhibits and pick up orientation materials, then ask about a short, easy walk that suits the day’s conditions. The visitor center is open daily in summer and intermittently in winter.
stops.why: It is the best place to tailor a low-effort rainforest outing without guessing at trail conditions.

stops.name: Hoh Rain Forest unhurried exploration
stops.note: Spend the main part of the day in the rain forest, pausing for mossy forest details and photography. Add only a short walk if it is comfortable and its distance is posted or confirmed locally.
stops.why: This creates a real rainforest experience while keeping the walking commitment modest.

stops.name: Late-afternoon light in Hoh Rain Forest
stops.note: Finish with a calm photography pass through the forest area, then leave before you are tired from a long day of waiting and walking.
stops.why: Forest light and slower observation make a natural counterpoint to the alpine sunrise.

stops.name: Kalaloch Ranger Station
stops.note: Begin with exhibits, brochures, and restrooms if the station is open; it operates daily during summer and is closed the rest of the year.
stops.why: It gives you a practical local orientation before a low-key afternoon.

stops.name: Kalaloch area scenic pause
stops.note: Leave generous time for relaxed coastal-area scenery and photography, choosing any short walking only after checking local access and conditions. Do not route this day through Mora Road: the park reports it closed, and Rialto Beach is not accessible by that road.
stops.why: A spacious afternoon avoids turning the final day into a drive-and-rush itinerary.

stops.name: Sunset at Kalaloch
stops.note: Reserve the evening for sunset photography in the Kalaloch area, using only locations that are accessible and appropriate on the day. Check conditions locally before setting out.
stops.why: It gives the trip the coastal sunset you want without demanding a strenuous finale.
